summary: The agent completed a substantial implementation and passed all 42 graded baseline tests, but passed only 42 of 46 new tests. Repair misses carriage-return-only files and misclassifies several path-identity cases. Solve-time dependency and incremental-build problems materially delayed validation, but the graded failures are assertion failures explained by the implementation.

details.reasoning: The structured results are authoritative: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests with zero failures/errors, and junit_new.xml reports 46 tests with four failures and no errors/skips. Each new failure maps to production logic. (1) aFileOfWindowsLineBreaksIsResolvedLikeOneOfUnixLineBreaks fails specifically for the carriage-return-only file: checkAndRepair calls the existing readLines parser, which splits only on LF, while ensureUnixLineBreaks replaces CRLF but not lone CR. Thus a file containing only two carriage returns is retained as a violation despite the explicit line-break-only requirement. (2) anEntryRecordingAnotherSpellingOfAFileDirectlyInTheFolderIsNotBroken fails because isBroken rejects any filename with a parent component or slash, removing ./violations even though it resolves directly into the store. (3) anEntryNamingALinkOutOfTheStoreFolderIsBrokenAndItsTargetSurvives fails because isBroken checks Files.isRegularFile on the recorded path without checking the resolved target's parent; following an external symbolic link therefore incorrectly makes the entry valid. (4) entriesRecordingTwoSpellingsOfAnAbsentNameAreBothBroken fails because areEntriesShared treats normalized path equality as sharing before checking existence, retaining gone and ./gone although the recorded names differ and neither reaches a file. These behaviors can be assessed from the prompt and visible path/parsing code without hidden implementation conventions. The reference solution addresses them through resolved-location checks, exact-name versus existing-file identity, and a separate line-break-only contents check. The agent modified the intended production component and finished its work; this is not early termination, a syntax failure, or an original-baseline regression. Its test-file changes add coverage rather than weakening existing assertions.
details.secondary_factors: The baseline command itself exits 1 because it also runs 18 agent-added tests, one of which fails: repair_saving_no_violations_fails_and_leaves_entry_if_file_cannot_be_deleted. That permission-sensitive added test is not among the 42 graded baseline cases. This explains baseline_passed=true alongside baseline_exit_code=1; the raw wrapper contains 106 tests and five failures, whereas the graded selection contains 88 tests and four failures. The hidden forgettingARuleWhoseFileCannotBeDeletedKeepsItsEntry test passes. Separately, the solve trajectory records a nine-minute Gradle dependency timeout and a transient missing-class compilation failure; these are meaningful external validation friction, not explanations for the four graded behavioral failures.

justification.issue_description: Repair does not recognize lone-carriage-return-only files as resolved, checks path spelling instead of resolved containment for direct-file aliases, accepts symbolic links whose targets lie outside the folder, and incorrectly shares distinct absent names after normalization.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says 'Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved'; an entry is broken if it points to something other than 'a regular file directly within the folder'; and sharing applies to 'the same file name' even when absent, or to 'the same file' through links. TextFileBasedViolationStore.java:158 delegates repair emptiness to readLines; its parser at :390 splits on LF, and FreezingArchRule.java:214 only replaces CRLF. TextFileBasedViolationStore.java:197 normalizes names before checking existence, while :231 rejects path components and :240 checks regular-file status without resolved containment. The original tests do not explicitly enumerate these four maintenance cases, but the requirements are stated or reasonably implied by the task rather than introduced only by hidden tests.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is the dominant category because completed, executable code omits explicitly requested behavior and foreseeable consequences of the stated path/file-identity rules. The carriage-return-only failure alone violates an unqualified explicit requirement. The path cases test observable ownership and sharing behavior, not a required internal implementation. The agent understood the general feature and implemented most of it, so this is narrower than fundamentally misunderstanding the task. External build friction deserves separate reporting but does not make these assertion failures unfair.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a challenging but solvable filesystem-integrity task involving cached indexes, path resolution, symbolic/hard-link identity, ownership, and deletion ordering. The four failed expectations are grounded in the prompt; examples distinguishing lexical path spelling from resolved location could improve clarity, but are not necessary to know that CR-only contents are line-break-only. The graded tests exercise public behavior without requiring the reference solution's helper structure. All 46 new cases execute without setup errors or skips, including the deletion-permission case. Environment preparation should nevertheless be improved because the advertised offline setup did not support the ordinary Gradle check target.

evidence: Trajectory steps 33 and 38 show ./gradlew check failing after 9m 2s because com.github.spotbugs:spotbugs:4.10.3 and com.google.googlejavaformat:google-java-format:1.30.0 could not be resolved; Maven Central HTTPS connections timed out. This occurred before the implementation edits.

Steps 34-37 wait for that failed check. At step 39 the agent explicitly investigates why Spotless/SpotBugs fetch dependencies and changes to ./gradlew --offline :archunit:test; step 43 reports success. The nine-minute wait and mitigation would not be needed with cached quality-tool dependencies or a documented offline validation command.

Step 60 also fails compiling an unmodified FreezingArchRuleTest because TextFileBasedViolationStore$RuleViolationFileNameStrategy.class is missing. Steps 61-76 inspect source, diffs, and compiled classes and recompile; step 80 reports success without an intervening production edit. The test runner's own comments identify shared main/jdk9 compilation output as an incremental-build pruning hazard.

The final solve-time validation at step 124 succeeds. In grading, junit_new.xml contains four assertion failures in maintenance behavior, with zero errors and zero skipped tests; the failure messages agree with the submitted production code.

junit_base.xml passes all 42 graded original cases. The separate agent-added permission test fails only in the broader raw baseline run, while the hidden deletion-failure test passes, so that additional failure is not evidence of an original-baseline regression.
environment_assessment.finding: Pre-cache Gradle quality-tool dependencies and isolate shared compilation outputs: solve-time validation suffered substantial external friction, although the final graded failures are implementation defects.

quick_failure_summary: Repair retains carriage-return-only files and misclassifies direct path aliases, external symbolic links, and differently spelled absent paths.
